title: Garlic Butter Pasta
shortDescription: Pantry pasta the rookies can nail
subtitle: Pantry pasta the rookies can nail
description: Pantry pasta the rookies can nail. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Boil the pasta
steps.instruction: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil (water should taste like the sea). Add spaghetti and stir once so strands don't stick. Cook 1 minute shy of package time — you'll finish in the butter. Reserve 2 cups pasta water before draining.

steps.title: Make garlic butter
steps.instruction: While pasta cooks, melt butter in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. When foam subsides, add garlic and swirl 45–60 seconds until fragrant and pale gold — not brown. If garlic darkens fast, pull the pan off heat for 10 seconds.

steps.title: Toss and finish
steps.instruction: Add drained pasta to the garlic butter. Toss vigorously, adding pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce clings glossy to every strand. Fold in Parmesan off heat. Taste — Garlic Butter Pasta should be rich, salty, and silky. Adjust with salt, pepper, and more butter if needed.

steps.title: Serve immediately
steps.instruction: Serve straight from the pot or transfer to a warm tray lined with foil. Top with parsley and extra Parmesan. This dish does not hold well on a steam table — call the crew as soon as it is tossed.

proTips: Assign one cook to proteins and one to sides — rookies stay on timing, not multitasking.
Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Garlic Butter Pasta with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Garlic Butter Pasta on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Pantry pasta the rookies can nail. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
substitutions: Any short pasta shape works — penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti.
